content:
I found what appears to be the exact same theorem in two files:

  • Mathlib.Data.List.TakeDrop:List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length
  • Mathlib.Data.List.Basic:List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length

Is there a reason for this or would a PR to remove the version from List.Basic be accepted? I believe the intention was to move the theorem to List.TakeDrop in this commit.
I don't think there's a good reason for literally the same theorem twice. PR welcome!
How did you find this? Does this strategy find more duplicates?
PR: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40422

I found through doc-gen data. MWE:

git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.28.0 \
    https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4 /tmp/mathlib && cd /tmp/mathlib
  lake exe cache get
  lake build Mathlib:docs
  python3 -c '
  import json, glob, collections
  locs = collections.defaultdict(list)
  for p in glob.glob(".lake/build/doc-data/declaration-data-*.bmp"):
      d = json.load(open(p))
      for x in d.get("declarations", []):
          if (n := x.get("info", {}).get("name")):
              locs[n].append(d["name"])
  for n, ms in sorted(locs.items()):
      if len(ms) > 1:
          print(n, ms)
  '

Here is the output of that command (note on 4.28):

CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderBaseChangeEpimorphisms ['Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Monomorphisms', 'Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.CommSq']
CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderCobaseChangeMonomorphisms ['Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Monomorphisms', 'Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.CommSq']
List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length ['Mathlib.Data.List.TakeDrop', 'Mathlib.Data.List.Basic']
My guess is that we can also deduplicate these IsStableUnderBaseChange and IsStableUnderCobaseChange instances. It is less obvious which one is canonical since the proofs differ.
Do these instances still exist on current mathlib? What are they called?

Yes, they are here: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/CommSq.html#CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderCobaseChangeMonomorphisms

and duplicates here: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Monomorphisms.html
Called CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderCobaseChangeMonomorphismsand CategoryTheory.Abelian.instIsStableUnderBaseChangeEpimorphisms
Wait, isn't the question actually "how can this even happen? import Mathlib should surely break if the same declaration is declared twice"?

Wait what? I can reproduce locally? I assumed this was a doc-gen bug. Whatever is going on?


Hover says the lemma is proved in the file which you import first.
@Jovan Gerbscheid does your script which spots duplicate lemmas work when the duplicate lemmas have the same name?
There's a similar issue involved in #mathlib4 > shake --fix causes elementwise to panic .
I think my script doesn't see this, because I think the Lean environment can only contain one of the two declarations. And as you saw, which one depends on the order of your imports.
Yeah, this is a known "feature" that you can provide the same theorem multiple times

Kevin Buzzard said:

Wait, isn't the question actually "how can this even happen? import Mathlib should surely break if the same declaration is declared twice"?

E.g.

import Mathlib

/-- error: `List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length` has already been declared -/
#guard_msgs in
theorem List.take_one_drop_eq_of_lt_length : 1 = 1 := rfl

but I guess in this case one file doesn't import the other?
The use case of this feature is for lemmas about a def that are autogenerated in two separate files downstream of that def
I don't understand that use case yet. Why does such a lemma have to be autogenerated downstream? And twice? You seem to find it useful, please enlighten me :-)

Maybe a silly question, but does this mean that if one has say three repos A, B, C, where C imports A and B, and A and B both have theorem foo but defined differently, then there will be no warning and the definition of foo in C will depend only on the order in which A and B are imported?
No, there is no error only if the two theorems have exactly the same type signature (condition which autogenerated lemmas always satisfy)

Michael Rothgang said:

Why does such a lemma have to be autogenerated downstream?

I believe this is a performance optimisation, but I would like to know myself

Rewriting lemmas (foo.eq_1) were generated on use (e.g. rw [foo]) since rw calls docs#Lean.Meta.getEqnsFor?, and as this comment in Lean says:

Equation theorems are generated on demand, check whether they were generated in an imported file.

But it appears that things have changed, since lean#3983 (Lean 4.12) equational lemmas are always generated (I think)

code

def foo := 3

/-- info: foo.eq_def : foo = 3 -/
#guard_msgs in
#check foo.eq_def

/-- info: foo.eq_1 : foo = 3 -/
#guard_msgs in
#check foo.eq_1

/--
info: equations:
@[backward_defeq] theorem foo.eq_1 : foo = 3
-/
#guard_msgs in
#print equations foo

docs#Lean.throwAlreadyImported is the function that throws an error when it detects declarations with the same name imported from separate files, but prior to it there's a check for whether the types match and they specifically call out equational lemmas.
So I think the answer is: this behavior is now unnecessary and can be deprecated. But I'm not sure.

Equational lemmas are "reserved". This means that they are not generated at first, but the lemma name is marked so that the user cannot accidentally add another lemma with the same name. The lemma is only generated the first time when you ask Lean for the lemma, e.g. by writing #check foo.eq_1.

In this case, it is a useful feature to let multiple files generate the same lemma.

I would argue though that for user-defined declarations, this behaviour is confusing.

Yaël Dillies said:

No, there is no error only if the two theorems have exactly the same type signature (condition which autogenerated lemmas always satisfy)

If now B imports A, then there is an error in B even with the same type signature (at least in my experiment)
Yes, absolutely. I forgot to mention it, sorry
Yes, this is presumably why lake shake (which changed imports) was breaking the build.
But I thought that shake was meant to remove imports. This breakage can only happen when adding a new import.
It rearranges imports :-)
But what's the advantage of rearranging if this adds imports instead of removing them?

I don't know the details but I did notice in #39155 that some files definitely got increased imports (you can see many examples here https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/39155#issuecomment-4416279744 ). The same is true for the new shake PR #40343, see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40343#issuecomment-4644097823
(Sorry for the spam, but I opened a thread about the shake thing Kevin noticed at #mathlib4 > shake --fix causes elementwise to panic; still gathering opinions on what's best to do there!)
